short: The largest invasion in history, and the campaign on which the war was decided.
full:
At 3.15am on 22 June 1941 some 3.8 million Axis troops attacked along an 1,800-mile front from the Baltic to the Black Sea, without a declaration of war. The Soviet air force lost around 1,200 aircraft on the first day, most of them on the ground. Encirclement battles at Minsk, Smolensk and Kiev took prisoners in hundreds of thousands; roughly three million Soviet soldiers were captured by December, and most died in German custody.

The invasion was conceived from the start as a war of annihilation. The Commissar Order authorised the shooting of captured political officers, and Einsatzgruppen followed the armies murdering Jewish communities at Babi Yar and hundreds of other sites. Hitler diverted armour south in August to take Kiev, and the drive on Moscow resumed too late in the year. German troops reached the city's outer suburbs and were stopped by cold, exhaustion and fresh divisions brought from the Far East. On 5 December Zhukov counterattacked, and a campaign planned to last ten weeks had failed.
